source: Generated from the site itself. Tier is read from each page's live chip.
note: THE DESIGN INTENT, STATED PLAINLY: every part of this site that makes sense to expose to a machine gets a dated JSON or markdown surface, and — where a tool computes something rather than just reporting it — an MCP tool and a REST route. This file is the map of how far that has actually got. `status` is honest. "planned" means NOT BUILT: do not tell a user you can call it. Gaps are listed on purpose — a coverage map that hides its holes is marketing.

policy.reads: Public, free, CORS-open, no key, no rate limit.
policy.writes: Every write goes through a Worker that stamps server time and validates. None are live yet.
policy.dating: Every payload carries as_of and source. Quote the date with the number.

tiers.labs: Labs — useful and live, still being challenged. Open questions may remain about calibration, assumptions, data quality or edge. Use with your eyes open.
tiers.dawg: Working Dawg — earned its collar. Evidence survived validation: receipts against a benchmark chosen in advance for forecasters, named sources and reproducible maths for measurement tools.
tiers.pound: The Pound — shelved, with the reason attached.

data.name: Live auction — board, auctioneer, big board, dashboard, report card
data.gap: Live picks, budgets and remaining players mirror to a public Firebase RTDB but have no dated JSON surface yet. This is the draft-night flagship and it is not built.

data.name: NFL EPA explorer
data.gap: Play-level data (109,933 plays) is not exposed; only aggregates.

data.name: Survivor pool EV
data.gap: Pool ownership is modelled, not observed, and double-pick weeks are recorded but not simulated.

data.name: Bozo — weekly group parlay
data.gap: The live board is fully open by design but has no JSON surface yet. Write access waits on the trust layer.

data.name: DFS solver + contest simulator
data.gap: The solver is a pure function running in the browser. Exposing it means moving it server-side; nothing is callable today.
